requirements.text: Provide a non-authorizing dry-run that computes closure bindings and reports missing or mismatched scope, context, and hash inputs before model launch.
Diagnose missing context classes and classify planned-new files separately from existing dependency omissions.
Expose frozen review and repair windows without changing the prohibition on reviewed-file mutation.

Recover dead or interrupted attempts through append-only stale/reconciliation events, use Windows-safe stdin/script transport instead of fragile multi-line py -c quoting, emit bounded no-progress heartbeat/timeout signals, and clearly distinguish retryable transport failures from semantic findings.
Preserve all existing authority, lineage, Artifact View, verifier, lifecycle, and envelope predicates.

Give Codex reviewers explicit read-only access to repository authority required by the frozen Artifact View while keeping the attempt directory as the only writable workspace and binding the exact access route in proof and launch evidence.

Generate and validate candidate exactEvidence from frozen Artifact View bytes and stop repeated identical malformed or stale-evidence retries at a bounded threshold without converting them into semantic findings.

Make Refactor Acceptance the deterministic owner of the semantic-review requirement decision from current candidate custody, changed paths, deterministic evidence, repository rules, knowledge bindings, protected/high-risk facts, and maintainer intent.
Define a closed, hash-bound review-trigger policy with hard-trigger precedence and fail-closed handling for unknown or contradictory risk facts.

Preserve the optional pre-implementation Bootstrap boundary: plan-ready plus explicit target-bound maintainer implementation authorization is sufficient unless a higher authority explicitly requires pre-review.
Provide a deterministic-only Acceptance route for complete low-risk evidence without creating review lineage, access proof, launch authorization, or semantic model execution.
Require typed post-implementation semantic assurance for workflow-control-plane and other hard-trigger changes while keeping profile selection and exact reuse hash-bound.
Preserve bounded review re-entry, focused repair verification, P2 current-run closure, typed later discovery, and the three-round hard limit.
Add a Bootstrap-owned concurrent discovery wave that runs the three isolated discovery roles under one semantic-round reservation and parent validation boundary.
Retry only failed discovery roles after transport failure, preserve successful formal outputs, reconstruct wave readiness from existing events and attempts, and consume no additional semantic round.
Preserve high-cost acknowledgement, protected-path approval, later discovery confirmation, manual-pause closure, and explicit fallback-model actions for every wave or route.
Use legacy-read/new-write compatibility for historical Bootstrap and Acceptance evidence without bulk rewriting or converting legacy decisions into current authority.
Add a deterministic plan-local implementation terminal predicate that is separate from plan readiness and Acceptance, never launches Bootstrap, and validates the complete declared consumer closure.
Add detached cross-skill composition fixtures for VDD authorization, Quick Dev implementation completion, Acceptance-owned routing, optional Bootstrap, and Acceptance finalization.
Record non-authorizing review performance telemetry for model attempts, round usage, focused verification, deterministic-only routing, wave wall time, retries, and finding yield.

Freeze validated deterministic Acceptance facts for semantic review so Bootstrap challenges meaning without repeating machine checks, while stale or inconsistent facts fail closed before reviewer launch.
Apply a typed, hash-bound semantic risk lens that prioritizes reasoning without reducing Artifact View coverage, reviewer isolation, severity policy, or evidence requirements.
Treat a valid clean discovery with zero findings from all required reviewers as a first-class successful outcome with no minimum finding quota, retry, or automatic second round.

Stop semantic review as soon as the current question is answered, keep focused-verifier failure on repair, and permit later full discovery only through the existing typed escalation and confirmation boundary.

acceptance.assertion: Dry-run output contains computed candidate, source, validator, Git, write-set, execution-read-set, and dependency-closure hashes without authorizing a run.
Dry-run fails with actionable field-level diagnostics when closure or context inputs do not match prepare authority.
Missing required context classes identify the class and accepted scope needed to satisfy it.
A nonexistent allowed production output is reported as planned-new, while a missing dependency remains a closure error.
Inspect output identifies frozen and repair-required windows and never authorizes mutation of a frozen review.
Dead event-backed attempts append attempt-stale before lease reconstruction, with no manual evidence rewrite.

Transport, malformed-output, stale-evidence, and semantic blocker outcomes have distinct retry guidance; Windows command transport avoids multi-line py -c quoting hazards and no-progress attempts produce a bounded heartbeat/timeout outcome.
Existing reviewer isolation, exact coverage, independent verification, lineage hard limit, and non-authorizing envelope predicates remain unchanged.

The shared Codex command factory expresses repository read-only access explicitly; reviewed repository paths remain outside every child writable root and no ad hoc wrapper or global user configuration is required.

Access proof and launch authorization bind the executable, model, effort, sandbox, read permission, environment class, Artifact View manifest, and attempt-only write root, and reject any drift before reviewer launch.
Candidate line ranges and exactEvidence are derived from the cited frozen snapshot bytes with CRLF/LF-normalized inclusive-line semantics and are validated before formal publication.

Repeated identical malformed-output or stale-evidence fingerprints stop at a declared retry threshold with append-only evidence and actionable recovery guidance; they consume no semantic round and authorize nothing.
Acceptance emits a deterministic required/not_required decision bound to candidate custody, changed paths, deterministic evidence, knowledge, and decision inputs.
Caller-supplied required/not_required text cannot override hard triggers, and the decision output carries reason codes, sources, hashes, profile, and authorizes=[].
Equivalent current input bytes produce equivalent review requirement semantics, while any bound input drift invalidates the prior decision.
The review trigger set is a closed enum with hard-trigger precedence, and explicit maintainer request can only upgrade to required.
Unknown or contradictory risk facts fail closed rather than defaulting to not_required.
A plan-ready target with explicit target-bound implementation authorization can enter Quick Dev without upstream Bootstrap evidence when no higher authority requires pre-review.
Plan-ready alone, stale or missing authorization, and fabricated Bootstrap evidence cannot authorize Quick Dev.
Complete low-risk deterministic evidence routes to deterministic_only without a lineage family, access proof, launch authorization, or model execution.
Deterministic-only Acceptance still publishes only its own non-authorizing evidence and leaves acceptance-passed to Acceptance.
Workflow-control-plane changes deterministically classify post-implementation semantic assurance as required.
The required decision selects an explicit typed review profile and does not widen exact finalized-run reuse across incompatible profiles.
Acceptance remains the only owner allowed to publish acceptance-passed after importing validated current Bootstrap evidence.
First semantic entry uses full discovery; a non-escalated P0/P1 repair uses one focused verifier; P2-only repair uses current-run deterministic closure.
Later full discovery requires a typed trigger, recommendation/confidence, explicit user confirmation, and hash-bound authorization; the full-review hard limit remains three and Round 4 is rejected.
One Bootstrap-owned discovery wave launches blind_hunter, edge_case_hunter, and acceptance_auditor concurrently with isolated attempts, handshakes, candidates, and formal outputs.
The wave parent validates each role independently and gates only after all required roles are terminal-valid; wave state is reconstructed from existing events and attempts.
A partial transport failure preserves successful formal outputs and retries only the failed role.
Role retry does not consume another semantic round or create a new review lineage, reviewId, or changeId.
A wave cannot reuse stale high-cost acknowledgement, protected-path approval, or later-discovery confirmation after cost, candidate, model, or run identity drift.
Manual pause and fallback-model actions remain explicit operator boundaries with no hidden provider dispatch.
Historical Bootstrap and Acceptance evidence remains readable and replayable under its frozen contract without mutation.
New writes use the current decision and profile contracts, while legacy decisions remain non-authorizing compatibility inputs.
The target-local validate_implementation.py is declared as the Quick Dev terminal predicate and is separate from validate_plan.py and Acceptance.
The implementation terminal predicate is deterministic, non-authorizing, does not launch Bootstrap, and checks all declared slices, consumer closure, tests, fixtures, and contract consistency.
Detached composition fixtures cover plan-ready authorization, Quick Dev implementation-complete, Acceptance routing, optional Bootstrap, and Acceptance finalization without authority leakage.
Composition fixtures cover low-risk deterministic-only, current-target required review, focused repair, later-discovery confirmation, partial wave retry, and clean-not-authority cases.
Review performance telemetry is append-only, hash-bound, non-authorizing, and cannot affect severity, routing, lifecycle, or release decisions.

Bootstrap receives a hash-bound frozen deterministic-facts bundle covering current tests, schemas, hashes, file existence, requirement coverage, changed paths, commands, and knowledge freshness without rerunning those checks as semantic work.
Missing, stale, or inconsistent deterministic facts block reviewer launch before semantic execution and never become a model finding.
A typed risk lens is bound into the review input and selects reasoning priorities for the active risk category.
Risk lens selection cannot reduce Artifact View coverage, change reviewer isolation, alter severity policy, or authorize sampling.
Three valid isolated reviewers returning zero findings produce a clean gate with no retry, minimum-finding failure, or automatic second semantic round.
Clean Round 1, P2-only closure, and a passing focused verifier each stop semantic review without opening another full discovery round.

A focused-verifier failure routes to repair and focused verification; later full discovery remains blocked until a typed escalation trigger, recommendation/confidence, explicit user confirmation, and hash-bound authorization exist.
